newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILE SHARES END LOWER AS WALL STREET SETS TONE.
newsitem.headline: CHILE SHARES END LOWER AS WALL STREET SETS TONE.

text.p: Chilean shares finished lower in thin turnover on Tuesday, with a slump on Wall Street setting the tone in the absence of local market-moving news, said traders.
Sluggish trading is expected to continue at the opening, with many investors taking advantage of the dearth of news and short trading week to review their portfolios, they said.
The bolsa will be closed Friday for a public holiday.
The 40-share .IPSA index unofficially ended down 1.01 percent at 131.02 points. The general .IGPA index shed 0.57 percent at 5,609.6 points.
Turnover rose to 9.6 billion pesos from seven billion pesos Monday.
"There's no relevant news so Chile is virtually a copy of what's happening in Wall Street," said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investment.

Telex-Chile slumped after media reports that its owners may sell a controlling stake in the telecommunications company, whose profits have fallen this year, said traders. Telex ended down 2.25 percent at 870 pesos.
Other decliners included the Chispa group of investment companies linked to Enersis, which continued to tumble on uncertainty over the impact of the recent deal with Endesa Espana, said traders.
Gainers included forestry company Masisa, up 1.16 percent at 217-1/2 pesos, Banco Edwards, up 0.47 percent at 53 pesos, and telecom Entel which rose 0.33 percent to 3,020 pesos.
